 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(t)

Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n{p.extract_text()}' for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))

strengths: The paper addresses an important problem: distilling high-resolution image datasets without unrolling student optimization. Feature representatives combined with class-specific BatchNorm regularization provide a practical pipeline.

Table 1 reports substantial improvements across several settings. At 50 images per class, the method achieves 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet versus CDA's 48.7%, and 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus 53.5%. Evaluation covers three datasets, multiple compression budgets, and three runs.

Cross-architecture experiments demonstrate useful transfer to larger ResNets. Ablations, regularization sensitivity analysis, and synthetic-image visualizations provide additional insight into the method's behavior.

The pipeline is generally clearly presented and credits its SRe2L, DeepInversion, optimal-transport, and POT foundations. The supplement appropriately acknowledges pretrained-model dependence and inherited dataset biases.
weaknesses: The central formulation's novelty is insufficiently established. With squared Euclidean cost and freely optimized support weights, Eqs. (7)–(10) reduce to classical k-means quantization: minimizing the average squared distance to the nearest representative. This equivalence is neither discussed nor evaluated against a k-means feature-target baseline, leaving the benefit of the barycenter machinery unclear.

The headline gains are not reconciled with the ablations. At ImageNet-1K 10 IPC, Table 1 reports 21.3% for SRe2L, whereas Table 3's stated CE-plus-standard-BN baseline reaches 36.1%, without explaining the discrepancy. Moreover, the full method improves over CE plus per-class BN by only 0.5–0.8 percentage points across the three datasets. These improvements can be useful, but matched baseline reruns are needed to establish which changes drive the larger reported gains.

The MMD comparison does not isolate the metric convincingly. At 1 IPC, the proposed optimal feature representative is exactly the class feature mean, also the target of linear-kernel MMD in the same feature space. Consequently, Section 5.5's geometric explanation for the 5.77% versus 0.48% result requires controls for feature extractors, BN regularization, and optimization. The broader criticism of MMD also conflates mean matching with MMD using more expressive kernels.

The connection between the mathematical objective and the evaluated dataset is incomplete. Algorithm 2 learns support weights, but Algorithm 1 outputs only images, and their use in student sampling or loss weighting is unspecified. The resulting empirical distribution need not equal the optimized weighted measure. Separately, the positive Hessian with a fixed transport plan does not establish the convexity claimed for the minimized transport objective in Section 4.2.2.

Important solver details remain unspecified: barycenter initialization, iteration count, step size, and handling of zero weights despite updates dividing by those weights. Algorithm 2 also updates the weights while reusing a transport plan computed under the previous marginals; the intended update order needs clarification.

The efficiency evidence is narrower than the scalability claim. Appendix F measures ImageNette at 1 IPC, where the barycenter reduces to a mean. It does not establish small transport overhead at ImageNet scale with 50–100 IPC or clearly separate teacher training, feature extraction, barycenter computation, and relabeling costs.
